topic.title: Amazon's cloud, servers rented to other companies, made $45.6 billion of Amazon's $80 billion operating profit in 2025, more than the whole North American store

title: Amazon's whole North American store made $29.6B. Its rented computers made $45.6B 🖥️
description:
How did Amazon's rented computers make $45.6B in operating profit in 2025, more than its whole North American store's $29.6B?
Sources: Amazon Q4 2025 results (Dec 2025). The characters are not advisers.
Illustrative only. Not financial advice.

Logo: Amazon.com, Inc., Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Amazon_logo.svg)
cta: Did you know Amazon was a cloud company? Comment

lines.text: Amazon's rented computers made $45.6B in profit last year.
Its whole North American store made less, only $29.6B all year.
Yet those computers bring in just 18% of Amazon's sales.
Who rents them? Companies running their apps and websites, on Amazon Web Services.
So why does the store keep so little? Every parcel needs a warehouse, a driver and a van.
From each sales dollar, the cloud keeps 35%. Amazon overall keeps 11%.
That's how rented computers made 57% of Amazon's $80B profit.
So is Amazon a shop, or a computer company?
